daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Stock Performance Rankings with Rolling Averages
daily_quests.description: Using the ASX 200 historical prices dataset, write a SQL query with window functions to: (1) Calculate the 20-day and 50-day rolling average closing price for each stock ticker, (2) Rank stocks by their price momentum (current price vs 50-day average) within each trading month, (3) Identify stocks that crossed above their 50-day average in the last 30 days. Use ROW_NUMBER() and LAG() window functions. Return: ticker, date, close_price, ma_20, ma_50, momentum_rank, and a flag indicating crossover events. Order by date descending and momentum_rank ascending.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning and Incident Type Classification
daily_quests.description: Download the NSW Road Crash Data from data.nsw.gov.au. Write a Python pandas script to: (1) Load the crash data CSV, (2) Clean missing values in critical columns (crash_date, location, severity, vehicle_type), (3) Standardise date formats and extract year, month, hour_of_day from crash timestamps, (4) Categorise crashes into severity buckets (Fatal, Serious Injury, Other Injury, Non-Injury) based on the injury_type column, (5) Remove duplicate records based on crash_id, (6) Export the cleaned dataset to a new CSV file with a timestamp suffix. Document any data quality issues found in comments.

daily_quests.title: Australian Weather Patterns: SQL Analysis + Python ETL Pipeline
daily_quests.description: Using the Bureau of Meteorology / Australian Weather observations dataset (available on Kaggle): (1) Write a Python script to download/load the weather CSV, perform initial cleaning (handle missing temps, standardise station names, validate date ranges), and load it into a local SQLite database. (2) Write SQL queries to: identify stations with the highest temperature variance by season, calculate the 3-month rolling average of rainfall by region, rank states by average maximum temperature for each month of the year using window functions. (3) Export SQL results back to Python, create a summary DataFrame showing top 5 hottest and wettest regions, and save as a formatted CSV report. Expected deliverables: (a) Python ETL script, (b) SQL query file, (c) Summary report CSV.
